attempts.summary: Built a double-NAT transit path: node3 (lan-a, RHEL7) sends HTTP requests to node4 (lan-b, RHEL7) on port 8080, via node1 (VyOS, SNAT #1 to transit IP) and node2 (OPNsense, SNAT #2 to lan-b IP). node4's HTTP access log confirms the connection is recorded as arriving from 10.50.30.254 (node2's lan-b address), not from node3 (10.50.10.12) or node1 (10.50.20.1). All four nodes were then restarted one at a time via native reboot, each showed a changed OS-native boot identity, and the full double-NAT path plus underlying config (interfaces, routes, NAT/firewall rules) was verified to have survived and recovered after each restart.
